Table SM12.1. The four preregistered Experiment 2 follow-up tests in the intention-to-treat follow-up cohort (as reported in the main text) and the per-protocol cohort, with both covariate versions of the assignment-based tests, both measures of immediate change for the persistence slopes, and the worst-case return imputation.

Note. DD = Debunking Dialogue; ID = Irrelevant Dialogue; IL = Information List. "ITT" = all believers of the intention-to-treat main-experiment sample (SM11) who returned to the follow-up survey; the follow-up preregistration specifies no exclusions, and this is the cohort reported in the main text. "Per-protocol" = returnees from the per-protocol main-experiment sample (i.e., excluding the six returnees whose dialogues were flagged for event denial). ANCOVA rows: follow-up outcome regressed on a DD dummy (Information List and Irrelevant Dialogue pooled) plus either the preregistered covariate (the pre-treatment rating of the participant's own conspiracy belief) or the pre-treatment three-item Kirk composite, entered as a linear covariate without interaction; HC2 SEs; d = b / SD of the outcome. Persistence rows: Lin et al. estimator (t 2t 0 ) ∼ b 1 (t 1t 0 ) + t 0 , with t 2 the follow-up outcome and t 0 , t 1 either the pre-and post-treatment Kirk composites (as reported in the main text) or the pre-and post-treatment ratings of the participant's own conspiracy belief; "worst-case return imputation" sets t2 = t 0 for every believer who did not return (complete decay of belief change) and refits the composite model on all believers with t 0 and t 1 observed.

The follow-up preregistration (AsPredicted #251092) names "pre-treatment ratings of respondents' own conspiracy views" as the covariate for the assignment-based tests, and the main text reports that model. Table SM12.1 also reports each test with the pre-treatment three-item Kirk composite as the covariate (the composite is the baseline measure that enters the persistence and mediation models); each covariate is entered linearly, without interaction terms. In the ITT cohort, LDS shooting beliefs give b = -0.46 (95% CI [-3.30, 2.37], p = .748) with the preregistered covariate and b = -0.07 ([-2.68, 2.55], p = .961, d = -.003) with the composite; generic conspiracy beliefs give b = -3.33 ([-6.57, -0.09], p = .044) and b = -2.92 ([-5.88, 0.04], p = .053, d = -.119), respectively. The minimum detectable effect on generic conspiracy beliefs at 80% power, computed from the standard error of the assignment coefficient in the ITT cohort as (1.96 + 0.84) × SE, is 4.6 points with the preregistered covariate (SE = 1.65 points; d = 0.19; power of roughly 33% for a true effect of 2.5 points and 44% for 3 points) and 4.2 points with the composite covariate (SE = 1.51 points; d = 0.17; power roughly 38% and 51%). The computation is reproduced by the deposited R pipeline.

Following Lin et al., the persistence analysis regresses follow-up change on immediate change with baseline controlled: (t 2 -t 0 ) = b 1 (t 1 -t 0 ) + b 2 t 0 + ε, where t 0 and t 1 are the pre-and post-treatment measures of belief in the Kirk conspiracy and t 2 is the follow-up outcome. Random assignment does not enter this model, so b 1 is described as the persistence of immediate belief change (identified under the assumption that, given t 0 , no unmeasured factor confounds post-treatment and follow-up belief), not as a treatment effect.

In the ITT cohort, with the three-item Kirk composite as t 0 and t 1 , b1 = .117 (95% CI [.02, .22], p = .019) for LDS shooting beliefs and .194 ([.08, .30], p < .001) for generic conspiracy beliefs (n = 851 returnees with all three measures). With the pre-and post-treatment ratings of the participant's own conspiracy belief as t 0 and t 1 instead (the measure named as the covariate in the preregistration), the slopes are .073 ([-.000, .146], p = .050) and .172 ([.090, .255], p < .001), respectively (Table SM12.1).

Table SM12.2 fits the persistence model separately within the Debunking Dialogue condition and within the pooled control conditions and tests whether the slope differs by condition. In the ITT cohort, the carryforward rate for generic conspiracy beliefs is nearly identical across conditions (b1 = .193 in the Debunking Dialogue condition, p = .003; .197 in the control conditions, p = .153; slope × condition interaction b = -.056, p = .71). For LDS shooting beliefs the control-condition slope is numerically larger (b1 = .104 in the Debunking Dialogue condition, p = .062; .262 in the control conditions, p = .037; slope × condition interaction b = -.199, p = .14), although the control-condition estimate is imprecise (95% CI [.02, .51]) and the interaction is not significant. Persistence slopes estimated on all returnees and separately within the Debunking Dialogue and control conditions, with the slope × condition interaction (intention-to-treat cohort, as reported in the main text; per-protocol cohort for comparison).

Note. Lin et al. persistence model (t 2t 0 ) ∼ b 1 (t 1t 0 ) + t 0 fit on all returnees (pooled), separately within the Debunking Dialogue (DD) condition and within the pooled control conditions, and with a DD dummy and its interaction with (t 1t 0 ) added (last column). Conventional OLS SEs, matching the published estimator. Returnees with t 0 , t 1 , and t 2 observed: ITT (872; main text): n = 851 pooled (442 DD, 409 controls); Per-protocol (866): n = 845 pooled (436 DD, 409 controls).

Selective return of the participants whose beliefs changed most would bias b 1 upward. The imputation that addresses this concern from the conservative side assumes complete decay of belief change for every non-returner: we set t2 = t 0 (a follow-up change of zero) for each believer with observed t 0 and t 1 who did not return (or who returned without a value on that follow-up outcome), and refit the model on all such believers (N = 1,017 in the ITT sample, of whom 851 are returnees with all three measures). Under this assumption every non-returner contributes evidence against persistence, however much their belief changed immediately. The slopes are essentially unchanged: b1 = .113 (95% CI [.02, .20], p = .015) for LDS shooting beliefs and .179 ([.08, .28], p < .001) for generic conspiracy beliefs.

Persistence was present in both arms, but far more change was induced in the treatment arm: among ITT returnees the post-treatment composite fell by 7.55 points on average in the Debunking Dialogue condition and by 1.31 points in the control conditions.
